subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram expose a public parse/text-mode config beyond existing `richMessages` and `markdown.tables`, and which modes, defaults, and per-account overrides should be supported?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested config surface is missing, but choosing supported modes changes public config, default rendering, and escaping/security semantics that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow text-mode config
options.body: Add a Telegram-plugin config that preserves current HTML by default and allows an explicit plain/no-parse opt-in, while treating MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom emoji as separate decisions.

options.title: Keep existing richMessages-only surface
options.body: Close or defer parseMode and document `richMessages: false` plus current HTML/plain fallback as the supported compatibility path.

options.title: Broaden into a formatting-design issue
options.body: Convert this into a larger maintainer-owned design covering MarkdownV2, raw entities, rich messages, custom emoji, and per-account behavior together.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow text-mode config
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-plugin config that preserves current HTML by default and allows an explicit plain/no-parse opt-in, while treating MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom emoji as separate decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest current-main routing candidate for the Telegram config/docs/send surface in this checkout.
